title: Upper Bound on the Correlation Energy of a Dense Fermi Gas in the Thermodynamic Limit
authors: Niels Benedikter, Sascha Lill, Marcello Porta, Benjamin Schlein
abstract: We prove that the random phase approximation provides an upper bound on the correlation energy of a three-dimensional, weakly interacting, Fermi gas in the thermodynamic limit at high density. More precisely, we consider a mean-field scaling regime where the kinetic and interaction Hamiltonian are scaled by $ρ^{-2/3}$ and $ρ^{-1}$, respectively. We use a correlated trial state constructed through a quasi-bosonic Bogoliubov transformation of collective particle--hole excitations associated to patches on the Fermi surface. Key of the proof is to control the position-space localization of the collective excitations. Combined with an iterated Duhamel expansion of the expectation values of (localized) particle number operators we obtain extensive estimates, which justify the reduction to an effective quadratic Hamiltonian and its approximate diagonalization.
summary: This paper establishes a rigorous upper bound for the correlation energy of a dense, weakly interacting Fermi gas using the Random Phase Approximation (RPA). The authors employ advanced techniques involving Bogoliubov transformations and Duhamel expansions to simplify the complex many-body Hamiltonian. The result provides a crucial theoretical benchmark for understanding quantum correlations in high-density quantum systems.
main_problem: To rigorously prove that the Random Phase Approximation (RPA) provides an upper bound on the correlation energy of a three-dimensional, weakly interacting, Fermi gas in the thermodynamic limit at high density.
main_result: The ground state energy density is bounded by the sum of the non-interacting energy density, the RPA energy density, and a vanishing error term in the thermodynamic limit.
method: The proof constructs a correlated trial state via a quasi-bosonic Bogoliubov transformation of collective particle-hole excitations, followed by an iterated Duhamel expansion to reduce the Hamiltonian to an effective quadratic form.
model_or_system: The system is a gas of $N$ fermions on a 3D torus $\mathbb{T}^3_L$, governed by a Hamiltonian involving kinetic and density-dependent interaction terms. The analysis focuses on the high-density scaling limit.
key_observables: Correlation Energy, Ground State Energy Density ($e_{GS}$), RPA Energy Density ($e_{RPA}$)
important_parameters: Density ($\rho$), Fermi momentum scale, Thermodynamic limit ($L \to \infty$), High-density scaling regime.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a mean-field scaling regime and relies on controlling the position-space localization of collective excitations, leading to the reduction to an effective quadratic Hamiltonian.
paper_structure: The paper systematically proceeds by constructing the correlated trial state, mapping operators to position space, bounding the number of excitations, reducing the Hamiltonian to a quadratic form, and finally extracting the RPA energy bound.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical treatment of correlation energy bounds in a Fermi gas is foundational for understanding strongly interacting quantum matter, providing theoretical benchmarks for comparisons with experimental results from ultracold atomic gases.
